utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning. One counsel is standing, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: A very small and practical matter, your Honour, I want to raise, that is, we were to file today a motion asking for additional or amended protection of our witnesses. I think we need another week, even less, but, nevertheless, we are not able to file it today as we said we will do so. So we ask an extension for the next Thursday because we will not sit on Friday.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, that is August 2nd, I guess. My, time is speeding. For some of us it is speeding. For me it is speeding. Any objection from the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. You may have that extension, Mr. Wladimiroff. Mr. Keegan, you were questioning Mr. Mujcic?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Regarding the decision on hearsay, I had indicated that would be prepared today. It is prepared almost, but it needs to go to the translators. That means we will probably be able to have it to you -- Miss Featherstone -- Tuesday, if we are lucky.

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: Tuesday, if we are lucky.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, Tuesday, if we are lucky, Wednesday perhaps. Once again, if counsel will have their comments regarding the witness whom we spoke about yesterday, if you will have your comments to us by the close of business today, then that matter will be expedited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: We have already passed our comments to Miss Featherstone, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. MR. ARMIN MUJCIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, you are still under oath. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Mujcic, when we broke yesterday you were describing how you saw the accused Dusko Tadic on a tank in the village of Kozarac during the attack. If I could have Exhibit 202 shown to the Defence which is a map of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: 221, is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It could be possible. I gave the wrong number. 221, excuse me. (To the witness): Mr. Mujcic, do you recognise what that Exhibit is, Exhibit 221?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What is that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It shows Marsala Tita Street which is now from the direction of Kozarac towards the main road of Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If that could be put on the Elmo, please? Thank you. Mr. Mujcic, using the pointer there and indicating on the map which is on the overhead, could you please indicate generally the location where you were when you saw the tank first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right here where the pharmacy and the textile shop was, between the park from the school and that building here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With relation to that building which contained the pharmacy and textile shop, where were you in relation to that building? In front of it, behind it, next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind it, around the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where was the tank at that time when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The tank was here across from here. Whether it was on the road or whether it was off the road where the pavement was, where the restaurant was, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You are saying "whether it was on the road", which road are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That road that led towards the intersection, towards the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. You are referring to Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What building was the tank in front of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we could run Exhibit 195 which is the film of Kozarac, please? Mr. Mujcic, when you see this film, what I would ask you to do is indicate the place where you saw the tank parked first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. What building is that we see in the picture here, the large building to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a building where the restaurant was, another shop and a shoe shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you move that picture up a few frames, please? Thank you. Is that the area where you saw the tank parked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe how it was parked again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was turned towards Kozarac. Whether in that moment it had come or stopped there, the engine was still running, I do not know. When I looked up it was standing still.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we fast forward through to the other side where the camera is coming back the other way on the screen? If you could slow it down, please? If you could stop -- keep going, please. If you could indicate when you see the building you were behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you could just back that up a few frames, please, to where you are there between the two? Right there, thank you. This is the building that you were standing behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Which end of the building were you on, this end or the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was standing on the other side around the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you now move forward to just the other end of the building, please? Stopping a few more frames please -- there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you standing, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right around the corner behind the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: From this position that we are looking at now, where was the tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Across from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that directly across?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps a little bit up or down, I do not remember exactly, but I could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was there anything obstructing your view to that tank with the people on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You can stop the tape now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The witness said that the tank was pointing towards Kozarac which tells me nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I am going to clear that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): Sir, you described that the tank was pointing towards Kozarac. When you said that, can you tell us whether you mean it was pointing down towards that triangle intersection or back up the road towards the mosque and Mrakovica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was off the side of the road towards Mrakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was the gun too pointing in that direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly whether it was exactly in that direction or a bit to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw this tank, where did you see Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that moment I saw him climbing off the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was happening in the area around the tank at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a group of people who were coming from the direction of Mrakovica, a group, you know, a column. I cannot quite say, but there were a lot of people right there at the tank. There was also the military, the Serb military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were the other Serb military people doing at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were escorting people downwards towards the road Banja Luka/Prijedor. They were cursing, "Balija mothers", "Ustasha mothers", and all those things I cannot remember, threats and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What type of people were in this column? Was it all men or were there women and children in this column as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were elderly women, children, all ages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated yesterday that a young boy approached Dusko Tadic. Did you know who that boy was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you see happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Dule slapping him. He, sort of, pushed him into the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you saw that, did you and your group surrender to this column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not dare surrender when we saw that they were beating people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was Dusko Tadic wearing on that occasion, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember he wore the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you recall whether or not he had a beard at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yesterday you also indicated that you recognised one of the other people who was with Dusko Tadic. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised Goran Borovnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe Goran Borovnica, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was of short build, thin, one eye was cross-eyed, sort of, was not right, sort of cross-eyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you recall what he was wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly whether it was a camouflage uniform or SMB. In any event, it was a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did your group do after seeing that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We turned back because as we were meeting people they said that there was some collection centre or something in Trnopolje, so we decided to go towards Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you make it to Trnopolje or were you captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who were you captured by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was captured by armed people in the village of Causevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the people who captured you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised one, a man in a camouflage uniform. He had a net over his face, some camouflage net. I knew that he worked in Elektro Prijedor, he was an electrician, and he played soccer in a soccer club. Since I also played soccer, that is how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you recall his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know what his ethnic background was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you were captured were you held in the local area for a time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there they just checked us there. They asked why are we shooting at them from Kozarac, why we joined Tudjman and such and they mentioned Alija Izetbegovic as well. I do not remember all those things very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you taken by this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to a school in Donji Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long were you held in the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly the time, but it was night. They told us -- they closed, they locked us in a room where there was a school, and they said that we should spend the night there and the next day we will go to Trnopolje on buses to join our wives and children, and if somebody tried to flee they would shoot at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The next day were you taken to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that night, I do not know what time it was, all of a sudden one could hear noise. The door suddenly opened and curses could be heard, "Where are those balijas?" "Get out fast one by one, hands up on your neck", so that everybody from my group came out. I was the last. When I came to the doorway I recognised one young man, my age, whom I knew. I think he was called "Dragan". He cursed my balija mother and all that. He said, "Hands up behind your neck". I said, "Why? We know each other". He again cursed something and said, "You killed my brother in Kozarac or wounded him" or something, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, when I did not raise my hands, he grabbed me by the collar. He called over some others, one or two of them, and they started beating on me. He hit me with a rifle butt from behind in my head, and said, "Come over here now". It was dark outside over there. He took me around the corner of that school or whatever it was, and he put a bullet in the -- and I thought that it was over now. I thought to myself, God help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then a voice could be heard saying to let me go, that they would first interrogate me and then see what to do with me. The others were already in the van. I was all bloody. Then he called out a young man on the van whom he also knew and told him to tell me not to make any trouble, not to try to escape because in that case they would cut my throat, they would kill me. Then we were put into that van, and we were taken by people wearing camouflage uniforms with the insignia saying, "Milicija", militia, "Krajina". In that van they beat us, they ill-treated us, threatened us and so took us in the direction of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your prior answer indicated that the man put the bullet in and then the translation did not pick it up. Did you mean to indicate that he had put the bullet in the gun and you could hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was an automatic rifle, and he put a bullet in the barrel so as to shoot, that is, he uncocked the gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So this group which came to pick you up and take you to Keraterm was a different group than those who had captured you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was a different group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you arrived at Keraterm what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they brought us to Keraterm we saw a number of buses waiting there, all full. We saw women and children and adult men. They brought us there, and we were taken off on to the pista next to that red building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long were you in the Keraterm camp for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were interrogated there and they transferred us down there to one of those halls, to one of those areas. I spent there a day, maybe a night, and it could have been the next night that I left, I do not remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: From Keraterm where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the evening, late in the evening, the buses arrived and we were told to board the buses. Some people enquired, asked, those Serb guards, "Where are we going?" and they laughed and said, "You are going to Trnopolje, to your wives and children". People, of course, scrambled to get on to those buses to take seats as quickly as possible. So that the buses were overflowing, hundreds of people were on those buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did these people think they were going to be joining their families at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did the buses actually end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a long drive they ended up at Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: On the way to Omarska did the buses stop in any of the villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were frequent stops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened to those stops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually they took people off buses. In all the buses there were two, sometimes three soldiers, Serb. They had some metal rods and also some wooden sticks. They beat, ill-treated, abused verbally. I recognised quite a number of those guards, but I cannot remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When people were taken off the buses in the villages, do you know whether any of those people got back on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some returned beaten up, bleeding. Some did not. From my bus I saw a young man from Kozarac being taken off. I do not know him. I do not know his name. He was -- he seemed to break down and he started screaming, shouting, "Brothers, what are you doing to us? Open the windows". At that moment the guard came up. He was somewhere in the middle of the bus, and the guard came from the top of the bus. He trampled over people and he struck him with a rifle holding it by the barrel. He struck him in the head. I saw the man fall down bleeding, and he started again imploring them to open the windows and why were they keeping us there. Then they took him off, took him out of the bus outside and all I heard were cries of pain and he did not return again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you arrived at Omarska what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived buses were unloaded one by one. It was slow going because one by one came off the bus with hands behind the head. On two sides lined up were Serb soldiers and policemen with those metal pipes, rods, wooden bats, rifles and each one had to bow to walk past them towards that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you beaten when you went through that cordon of guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was impossible to get by all those people without being hit by a rifle butt, by a bat, by a baton, by a foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In what building were you placed in when you arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were put in that red hall, that room with stairs. It was called room 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you would, sir, if you could, please go around and using the pointer indicate on the model where room 15 is? Mr. Mujcic, if you could approach the model and by using the pointer indicate the room which you called room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is here by that entrance ------

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can barely hear the witness. Could you please direct the microphone towards him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, when you are describing you are going to need to lean towards the microphones on the table so that the translator can hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We entered through the staircase. There were also soldiers there beating us. Then we entered through this door here. This room was overcrowded with people already. They were loading us, piling us, almost one on top of the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you please point to the room again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model.)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you please identify that room by the letter and number designator which is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You have indicated there the number B23 which on the diagram appears to be a separate area within the room marked B7. Do you recall what was in that area, the one marked B23?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were toilets and wash rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In the small area across from that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were taps to wash hands and troughs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was that entire area, the area B7 as well as B23 in the other room, considered one room by the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat, please. How long were you in that room for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent there all the time until the interrogation, some 15 or 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe the conditions in that room? Was it crowded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it was overcrowded with people. People were lying in those toilets, in those water troughs or under those troughs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was there space for everyone in that room to be able to lie down and stretch out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we could hardly sit properly, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How frequently were you led out of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After three or four days that was when we were given food first. That was the first time that we went out and we went out only when there were meals. It also depended on the guard to let you go to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So that you were not always allowed to go to the toilet when you needed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was dangerous because it did happen that people would be beaten because they had stayed there a minute or ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Stayed where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When people were not allowed to use the toilet what did they do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they relieved themselves in those toilets where they were staying, where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were those toilets operating correctly enough to enable the conditions to remain sanitary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were all plugged. It was only some plastic bags or some old footwear we used to relieve ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How often were you given water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That depended also on the guard. If some -- when some people had some money, marks or something else to pay for it, then they would bring a canister, a can of water, which of course was not enough for even half of the people to quench their thirst.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were people becoming ill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you yourself become ill in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dysentery -- we all had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken and they would come, policemen or soldiers, to take us to the building which had the restaurant downstairs, the kitchen, and on the upper floor there were offices and there they conducted interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you beaten on the way to your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, even at the entrance, up the first staircase there was a soldier, there is a kind of a dome or a vault over that staircase, a plate, and I would go, walk past him and he hit me several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In which building is the staircase that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in the building in which the restaurant was and where interrogations were conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Looking at the model in front of you, can you see that stairway on that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the place where he hit me, not the one who was escorting me, but another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that the circular area on the front of that building facing the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the model). It is where I have just pointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you were taken upstairs were you interrogated in one of the offices?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you beaten during your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the entrance when I was about to enter that office, the one who was escorting me, he struck me with a police baton from the back. He hit my head and said, "Mind what you are saying. If you don't tell everything, you know what awaits you".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you know who your interrogator was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gentleman told me his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What name did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was Rade Kovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After he introduced himself, did you recognise who he was, what he did for his occupation before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did recognise him. He was in the Kozarac National Park, the Manager, or had some executive position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know why he introduced himself, why he told you his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he told me his name because he knew where my home was and he knew my grandfather, and that not far away because my house was very close to those Serb houses and that his aunt was there whose name was Vida.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What type of questions did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he generally asked me about the rifle, which formation I belonged to, and that he knew my grandfather who was a resistant fighter, a partisan, so why was I, as an Ustasha, here; why I sided more with them, that I was not pro-Yugoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you own a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The group that you were with when you were captured, were any of those people armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How were those people dressed, the group you were captured with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The group that you were with when you were captured, how were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were all in civilian clothes. There were children and elderly, except that we were all wet because of the water since we were trying to hide in waters and those canals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you taken to after your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the building which housed the workshop. It is this big red building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The same building you had been in before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, another section of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Again could you please approach the model and point to the area to which you were returned after your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the model). It was this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just a moment we have to wait for the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model). This is where I was, by this door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, we have lost the picture. Can you identify the room you were in by the letter and number designator which is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I notice outside that room there is a corridor and a stairway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is where we entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That corridor and that stairway, was that area considered by the prisoners to all be part of one room with B14?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, one question: which is the corridor now and the stairway? I am trying to look at the model at the same time that I am looking at that view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you point to the corridor and can you point to the stairway, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What is the number and letter designator for the corridor, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Corridor, B16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat. How crowded was that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was packed with people. Once somebody counted, actually calculated the square footage, so it was about one half metre per person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were there ever guards posted up there on that first floor in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where was the normal guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the large hall, near the dumper trucks. They had their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you say "large hall", do you mean the large garage area, the main garage area, of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you see Dusko Tadic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you see him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you see him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him in the garage when he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were you doing down in the garage area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I had dysentery and at that time you have to go to the toilet all the time, and since I was upstairs, I could not come down over people all the time because some people did not allow that because they had to get up in order to let somebody pass. So that I asked, and another two young men who also suffered from it, we asked the guard to be outside near the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where was the toilet located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The toilet was located in the garage, up towards the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You say the "entrance", is that the door from which the prisoners went in and out of the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It was on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, ground floor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe the situation when you saw Dusko Tadic? What happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if you would mind getting the witness to actually point out the toilet?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I was going to, your Honour. I was going to describe it all first and then point it all out. (To the witness): Could you describe the situation when you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were sitting on a wooden box or crate near that room where we were otherwise in on the ground floor. I returned from the toilet and I was sort of about -- I was holding my hands over my stomach. In that moment the guards that were there in that area, otherwise it was a quiet day, the shift was, I cannot say that they were good but they were correct. They said, "The coloured ones are coming". We knew what that meant. That meant that we had to disappear that very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the term that the guards used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Sarenci" which means "coloured ones".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What does that term mean to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lot of visitors came in those camouflage uniforms which were coloured, often -- they often came to beat us, to take somebody out that they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So "sarenci" meant multi-coloured ones, meaning people in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you heard that what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What else would we do? Just run away as quickly as possible. So we started running towards the door of our room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened when you got to the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was already something going on there, as if people had heard, as if they too had heard, so there was a lot of people in front of the door, so that I was near the door, I could not get in. People were jumping off the lockers, the ones that were there. In that moment I looked whether I was going to be caught up by that group that was arriving and when I turned I saw .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of the toilet a group of people is coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone in the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In that moment I recognised Dusan Tadic, Miso Radulovic, a teacher from Kozarac, and Vujcic, I think his first name was Rajko, who was a bus driver of the Autotransport Company from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How was Dusko Tadic dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform. As much as I could remember at that time, he had a white police belt, dark sunglasses and a cap on his head which had a Kokarda or white eagle on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you do after you looked at this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That moment the place had already cleared and people were running up towards the room where I was, because whenever something happened they would all -- those who were closest to the door were most exposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How far into that room were you able to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all packed up to, up the stairs, so I came to the first landing and I could not go any farther. I was telling people to move so that I could go to my spot but it was too packed, I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sir, if you could approach the model once again and indicate first, please, where you were sitting? Just one moment, sir. We have to wait for the monitor to be switched on. All right. If you could indicate first where you were sitting, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model). I was sitting here on a wooden crate next to which there was a small, low wooden bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you could indicate where the door to your room was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you could indicate once you were at that door where it was that you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly. I know that he had passed the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. In that case can you indicate where the toilet is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model). I think it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did the Court get that location?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir. You can return to your seat. Sir, once you got into the room, to the landing, what do you recall happening next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A short time after that names were being called out, Hrnic Jasmin called "Jasko" was called out, Emir Karabasic, a policeman, and Eno Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After those people were called out did you see any of the events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I could see, Jasmin Hrnic and Karabasic were downstairs before, had come out before. They started beating them. I think that that was the group that had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You mean the group including Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe what the bus driver Vujcic looks like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was around 30, 30 something, tall and balding. I knew him because he was driving the bus on the line Prijedor/Omarska, and that was a bus with that extension and he also was doing the line to Mrakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did he have light or dark hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you recall whether he had a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A beard?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, he did not have a beard or no, you cannot recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not remember that -- he did not have a beard.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Is this the bus driver you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): What could you hear happening in the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard blows and then wails.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you hear music that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Music was played very often, but I cannot remember if that day, I do not remember even whether I ate that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you continue to watch the event for as long as you possibly could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until they were taken towards the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were you thinking during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought that we were all going to be tortured like this, that I wished that they would just kill me with a bullet -- it would be easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you recall whether anyone else was called out of the room after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were calling out, with these they called Eno Alic, but he at that moment did not want to come down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How was Eno Alic actually called out? Who called him out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they were calling him out in that moment he did not come down. He said, "He was going to kill me, he was going to kill me" as if he knew who was down there. I assumed it was somebody from the room 15 because there was a door and some messages were passed on pieces of paper so you could talk, that somebody already had said something. But when Eno Alic's father came ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After those three were called out, after the beatings, were others called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew about Jasmin and Karabasic. They were called out and then Eno later, when his father called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After that group were people called out to move the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but that took a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes. Did you see who was actually called out to move the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that they asked for volunteers to pick up the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you know or could you tell if anybody responded to the call for volunteers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Volunteers, no. In that moment I think I saw that people who were close to the door there at the entrance, that they took them, but who it was, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Later, after those people left the room, did you manage to move upstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when those screams happened there was silence. You could hear everything from outside, begging to be killed, not to be tortured. Blows were resonating. There were some heavy objects and then at one point there was such screaming that everybody just pushed upstairs to those rooms when people ran in from outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you see any of the people who came in from outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you see ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: -- two people who are referred to in this courtroom as G and H?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What do you remember about Mr. G?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Person G ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Describe what you saw of the two people who came up. Describe what they looked like without using their names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know the order in which they came in, but I know person H was naked, as far as I could see, down to his waist. I could not say about the rest. He was all smeared with oil. He was holding his hand over his mouth. He was throwing up. A person J also came and he was also vomiting and holding his mouth, and his mouth was full of blood and there was some hair and then I also saw some oil. Then another one came, I think his name was Mujkanovic. He was also pale. He also looked frightened and he was holding his hand up to his mouth and he was vomiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not Mr. Mujkanovic had any oil on him as the other two did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly. I did not know notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw these individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Keegan, the translation was Mr. "J" as in -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. That was in the switch and it was clear that they did not catch the letter. Did you mean to say Mr. "J"? or Mr. "G"?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He said "G" before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: He did, your Honour. He, of course, is going by the letters which I gave him and -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yesterday, I think it was Mr. Wladimiroff gave -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: We can pass names, if you would like, your Honour, if it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have altered that. Excuse me one minute, please. Do not give it to the witness yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I crossed off the letters, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just let the Defence see what you crossed off, though you are not concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am not concerned, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I am sure he did not write the witness a note. He did not write that long! OK, very good. (To the witness): You will open that and put it flat on the table.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those are the ones.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What ones, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Are those the two individuals whom you described seeing come up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. Where were you when you saw these individuals come up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they ran in and at such speed that they all pushed us all. We were all packed against the wall, up the stairs and against the wall, so I climbed up. I was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where upstairs were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the corridor.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, Judge Vohrah has just raised a question as to the note that was given to you with names on it and then the question was asked of you, "Who were they?" and you said, "The persons who came up the stairs". Were those persons G and H?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes, please. (11.30 a.m.) (The Court adjourned for a short time) (12.00 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, would you like to begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Mujcic, do you know a man named Duca Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, his home was two or three kilometres away from mine. I know him. He worked as a waiter in a coffee bar in a restaurant in Kozarusa. This restaurant belonged to the soccer club in which I played.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was he also involved in soccer tournaments in which you played?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He defended at tournaments. He was a goalman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe him, please, physically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was tall, big.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was he a strong man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What colour hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot quite remember. I know he combed it backwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you recall whether it was dark or light?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, light, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Would you ever have confused him for Dusko Tadic, physically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not because I know them both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In your opinion, would a person who knew either both of them or simply one of them confuse the physical appearance of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so. Tadic is shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there anyone who lived in the Kozarac area who looked exactly like Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ever see anyone in the Kozarac area whom you mistook for Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of anyone else in the Kozarac area talk about someone who looked exactly like Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of anyone else talk about mistaken identity, mistaking someone for Dusko Tadic because they looked exactly alike?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not think so. I think that in Kozarac quite a number of people knew Dusko Tadic and could not mistake him for anyone because he was a well-known person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know of a Mico or Miso Danicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the first time I hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, have you seen television programmes concerning allegations against Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some fragments I saw. I think Monika Gras, a film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that a film concerned with Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And contained interviews with G about what happened in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And H about what happened in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Other people talking about what happened in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see the arrest of Dusko Tadic on national television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the arrest, I did not watch it. I only heard it in [redacted], in [redacted] papers, that he had been arrested but nothing else, the circumstances or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see his photograph in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You did not hear then about the arrest of Dusko Tadic on television news?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that, but in [redacted], since I do not understand it, I could barely understand anything -- only the name and the surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, things that have been on television concerning events within Omarska have been of interest to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really. They would not be of interest to me because I more or less knew all that went on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have journalists asked to interview you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mrs. Monika Gras came to that building where I was. Other people gave interviews. I did not want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When that afternoon these events occurred in that large garage in Omarska, did you speak with others about what had happened? Were you told things by other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have, naturally. I heard it. Everybody talked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you speak to G about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard, I heard something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that from G?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, I do not remember -- well, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But the man we call H, you did not speak to him, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you think that there had been four people who were required to be volunteers from the inmates to go out into the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you think that those four people had been selected from that room which is the hallway at the bottom of the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was logical for me to think so because these people were already there. It was their place, the place where they stayed, and they did not enter upstairs to take people out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you think that G had bitten the testicles of Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That afternoon you have told us that you were not in the area of room 15 because of your illness. You were in the area of the wash rooms or lavatories because of the dysentery that you were suffering from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not in the area of room 15. This is another room where I was. In room 15 I was before the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, the large room on the other side on the ground floor. Can you remember the number of that room that was at the end of the corridor where you were placed after you had been interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in a room upstairs on the upper floor after the interrogation, not downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because all these rooms in this area have numbers over the doors, do they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were sitting on a wooden crate against the wall of the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you there on your own or with the two other people who were also suffering from sickness as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were two men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were all of you sitting on the crate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that I was sitting on that crate. There was also a low bench. It was hard for me to sit on the bench because I was also already sick and it was difficult for me to stand up, but from a crate, since it was somewhat higher, it was easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The guards who were on duty, their position was down in the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they -- some were across at a table, I cannot really be more definite, perhaps across or a little bit to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour. I apologise for interrupting, but this is a matter of redaction, some locations given; the times being 12.07.02 and 12.07.30. I think that the name of the location was mentioned three times. It would be page 27, lines 12 and 18.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was waiting for it to come up on the screen. Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is no objection at all, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It will be granted. Here it is. It will be granted. I assume you have the times correctly? Let us see. Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): I was asking you, Mr. Mujcic, about the place where the guards who were supervising this part of the hangar, where they were placed that afternoon before the men in the coloured clothing came to the hangar. I had suggested to you that they were in the area of the garage. You have told us that they were sitting at a table. Can you tell us where that table was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say the exact place because there were dump trucks there and they had a table. I do not remember if they were sitting at it or whether they were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the position of this table is in the area that we have described as the garage with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that near the door that was the main entrance from the back of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am just interested in where the guard was positioned who told you that the men in the coloured clothing were coming. I want you, if you can, to identify where the guard was who gave you that information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I cannot help you because I was bent over. I had -- the pain was very bad, so I was bent down. My head was down. At the moment when we heard the word "Sarenci", the mottled ones, I did not think where the guards were but only where the door was so as to run through it before they arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that what you did -- got up and run from that crate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right. That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you got up and ran from that crate, you ran away from the door that was the entrance into the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was running towards the entrance into my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, which is the opposite direction from the entrance from the back into the garage, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was running towards the room where I had been placed -- it is not far away -- and the column was coming from the direction of the WCs which were to the left, or from the direction of room 15, I could not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the guard shout this out to you, that the men in coloured clothing were coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they said, "Sarenci", mottled ones. That day there was a shift which was, well, one might say decent. They did not ill-treat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you quickly ran to the door to the hallway beneath the stairs that led up to the first floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You tried to make your way as far as possible from that door so that you could avoid having any contact with these men, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, since the door was practically bottle necked, people were jumping off the lockers and everybody was in front of the door, so those two had got to the door before me so that I remained outside the door, and at that moment, just afraid, afraid that the column might have arrived already and I could be caught. I cast a look in that direction. The column had already passed by, that is, I think they had already had passed by the toilets and then I looked up and I told you what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, you recognised, you said, three people who were within that column of men, is that right? About how many men are we talking about entering into the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were more than three.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you cast that glance up, presumably, you tried to get into the room through the doorway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, naturally, I was trying to run into the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you succeed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I succeeded. Some people remained upstairs. There were people who stayed by the lockers, but the majority had got up the stairs, jamming them so they could not reach my place. I reached the first landing of the staircase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you had cast that look up and you saw the column of men by the toilets, you then focused your attention upon getting into that room behind the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. My look was when I glanced to see if they were not too near to me. As I have said, they had already passed by the toilets but they were not near me, so that I did not feel I was really absolutely pressed to get in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you tried to get in that room as soon as possible, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but, nevertheless, I had enough time to see who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were looking for any gap in that room that you were trying to get into so that you could get away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no room. I was outside the door. These people already were at the door and I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were trying to force your way through those people who were at the door so that you did not remain on your own in the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to wait first for people to move away, to make some room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were looking at the space that they were going to give you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot ask for a space when it is all crowded, when you cannot get through. I was simply pushing with my hands those so that I would enter as quickly as possible and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You cannot ask for a space, you were trying to find a space?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And what else would I do -- tell somebody, "Excuse me, please, can I get through, can I get in"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that glance that you said you gave to the men in coloured clothing who were coming into the room, you describe the man whom you say was Dusko Tadic as wearing sunglasses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And a hat with a Kokarda badge on the hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or eagles, white eagles, I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what colour hat that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have that much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The clothing this man was wearing was what kind of clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember any colour of any belt that may have been on that uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really affirm that, but I guess it was white of the military police, or was it a new belt which would be of a light colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is the answer to that that you do not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of those two things -- it was either white or it was a new belt which had not been worn yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the man's face was he wearing a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible a day's growth or two days' growth, but I cannot claim that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you remember giving a description of this man in 1994 when you said he had sunglasses and a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible that he had a beard, but not a big one because when one does not shave for a day or two, he already has a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I was asking was, do you remember giving a description of this man in 1994 when you said he had sunglasses and a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I told you there in the court, that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am just asking whether you gave this description about two years ago, that he had a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say that he had a beard. I said, perhaps, he did have a beard but not a real beard. He was simply unshaven. He had not shaved for a day or two. I could not really see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you read that statement recently before you came into this court to give evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would like to look at a copy of it in your own language? This will be D25, your Honour, which I tender and I believe the Prosecution have a copy of this in Serbo-Croat; Mr. Keegan tells me he has. (To the witness): If you turn to page 4, Mr. Mujcic, you will see -- just read this to yourself -- two-thirds of the way down the page the names listed, Jasmin Hrnic, Emir Karabasic and Eno Alic, but there is a paragraph above there in which you give a description involving the sunglasses. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is from this statement here that I ask you the question about whether the man had a beard, because it says here, does it not, that that is what he had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it is written here, maybe I said it, but here I am telling what kind of a beard it could be. For me, a beard of one or two days, it was not like this long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you trying to alter the appearance of that man because you have heard other evidence in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not trying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I suggest to you is this, that that man was not Dusko Tadic, that you have mistaken the identity of that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Had I not known him, I could have made a mistake, but since I knew him, both with a beard and without beard, and since he has a strong dark beard if he does not shave for a day, I think that is already a man with a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But when you went upstairs were other people saying to you, "It is Dule, it is Dule"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not saying it was Dule, but when I got into the room people were already scared as if they knew who was there and what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So was there a rumour going around from people who did not know, who said that it was Dule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I have heard in that room, in room 15, that Dule was already there and only a door separated us from that room, so that people already knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So there was talk in that room upstairs from people who had just been upstairs, not been outside, that said it was Dule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could not talk and we did not feel like talking. We were all afraid. My opinion is that somebody heard from people and I conclude that based on when Eno Alic was called out, he appeared to have known who was looking for him. He was scared and he said, "He is going to kill me".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You did talk and others were talking about this man whilst you were upstairs in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us you talked to G?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is possible when he came back later after everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: One other area that I want to question you about and that concerns your seeing Dusko Tadic in Kozarac after the shelling of Kozarac. Do you remember telling the Court about that today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that he was on a tank that was stationary outside the restaurant building which you have identified in Marsala Tita Street, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember also saying in interview, this interview, that Dusko Tadic was wearing a mask and rode through Kozarac standing on a tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I said that he had a camouflage uniform. I do not remember any mask. I do not remember saying anything about any mask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Putting that on one side then, can you remember saying that he rode through the town standing on a tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said here that at the moment when I saw him I did not remember whether the tank was moving or just stopped there. I knew it was stationary. Maybe it had just arrived. There was a noise of the engines running.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You said that it was stationary and that he jumped off and hit a young boy and you have not read this statement, as you have told us, before you gave evidence in court here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Maybe you would just like to turn to page 6 of that statement and have a look. You will see the third paragraph down from the top of the page where it begins "Answer". It is right it appears that you said then in '94 that he rode through the town standing on a tank? Was that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that that is how I put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right, and is it the case here that after all that has happened to you, you are prepared to make up things to incriminate Dusko Tadic because you want some sort of revenge against him or the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, I am not accusing Dusko Tadic. The Tribunal is accusing him, and if I wanted to exact revenge on Serbian people I would have gone to the Bosnian Army and I would not have stayed where I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just briefly, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: This statement, Mr. Mujcic, which Mr. Kay is referring to, first off, the translation you are reading is not an original version of Bosnian which you yourself gave or signed; that is a translation of a translation, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you gave that interview, you gave that interview to officials and what you said was translated by someone else into another language, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You yourself did not produce a statement in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What is the term that you use to describe camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maskirna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: This interview, did that last for a long period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly what time, from the afternoon until the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Are these events which you enjoy talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you answer the questions you were asked to the best of your ability?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked me there both what I saw and how things happened in those situations in general, all the situations that happened there, so that I gave a statement about what I heard from other people and my personal experience of what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you like to look at the [redacted], Mr. Mujcic, and identify your signature on each page as well as corrections made by you to the text, and your signature confirming that the matter had been translated, read and approved by you in the Serbo-Croat language and you were happy with the interpreter? Thank you, Mr. Usher. Just look at that page that is open -- keep it open, please. It is your signature at the end of the interview, is that right, the signature of a man you were happy to have as an interpreter? If you want to go through the earlier pages you will see your signature on all the pages, some corrections by you to the text as well, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember all these changes here in [redacted]. They said, "Sign here" and I did. The gentleman who was translating, he was a Serb. I accepted him. I did not know that I had a choice or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan? I have one question. Mr. Kay asked you a question, Mr. Mujcic, as to whether or not you had said in the statement that Mr. Tadic was wearing a mask. Then there was no reference to anything in the statement regarding your having said that he was wearing a mask. Would you look in that statement or, perhaps, counsel can tell me. Did he say in the statement he was wearing a mask?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I accept his explanation that "mask" and "camouflage" are similar expressions and Mr. Keegan makes an entirely valid point there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. That was the word that the witness used for "camouflage"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. There was a question about did any of the perpetrators -----

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Keegan, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: There was a question whether any of the perpetrators wore a mask. The answer was, describing Tadic, and that term was translated as "mask" which was the point in the statement that there are inaccuracies.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That term in Serbo-Croat means "camouflage"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Thank you. Do you have any questions, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Mr. Mujcic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, you are permanently excused. You may leave now. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
