utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, at some stage I wonder if you could get a witness to explain, to me at least, what a Kokarda is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It is a term frequently used and I just do not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Also, I am not going to ask about the uniforms, but I meant to ask one of the witnesses yesterday, who worked in Omarska and I believe he lived in Kozarac, and we have heard testimony about the distance between Prijedor and Kozarac. I am not sure that we have heard testimony about the distance from Kozarac to Omarska. I wanted to ask the witness how many kilometres it is from Prijedor to Omarska and how long it would take to drive that distance under normal conditions. I do not know that we have that in evidence yet, certainly the distance from Kozarac to Omarska, but we may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The two questions, mine and Judge Stephen, have nothing to do with each other, but it was just a gap. Miss Hollis, would you call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Elvir Grozdanic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. ELVIR GROZDANIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that will be given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Elvir Grozdanic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gornji Garevci in the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: March 17th 1972.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you indicate that you were born in Gornji Garevci in opstina Prijedor, were you born in a village in the area that is generally referred to as Gornji Garevci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What village were you actually born in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grozdanici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time if I could have Prosecution Exhibit 79 provided to the witness? Mr. Grozdanic, if you would take a moment to look at that map to orient yourself and to locate Grozdanici on that map. If that map could be placed on the overhead projector, please. If you could point to that, please. Just a moment while we have to switch over to the overhead projector. Thank you. So that is a Grozdanici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us please, this larger area called Gornji Garevci, what was the nationality or ethnic group of inhabitants of that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the village of Grozdanici, what was the ethnic group or nationality of the inhabitants of the village of Grozdanici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, what is your nationality or ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far is Grozdanici from the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far is the village of Grozdanici from the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also around 8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you attend primary school both in Gornji Garevci and also in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you perform military service from March 1990 until March 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As part of that military service did you serve as a military policeman in Stip, Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you return to Grozdanici after you completed that military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you work as a full-time policeman from September 1991 until the attack on Kozarac in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you perform those police duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes in the town of Kozarac and on different parts.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what other parts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gornji Garevci, Kozarusa and Jaruge.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were at this time working full time as a policeman but you were a Reserve Policeman, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were your duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My duties were in Kozarac to control traffic and to patrol Gornji Garevci, Kozarusa and Jaruge.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you issued weapons as part of your duties as a full-time policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of weapons were you issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to taking this job as a policeman at Kozarac, did you ever go into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you go into the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you go into the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to school every day, and during the break three times a week.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then after you completed school, how often would you go into the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went three times because I played soccer in Kozarac, so we went to practise and to play games.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would be three times in what period, a week, a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A week.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the main business street in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know many of the people who had businesses and homes on that main street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many years had you known Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around 10 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him as the first time he was my karate trainer of the club in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While he was your karate trainer, how often would you have classes with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice a week I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to these contacts when he was your karate trainer, what other kinds of contacts would you have with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As passers by.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you say on an average you would see Dule Tadic in a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around, before I trained karate about two, three times, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then after you trained karate, how often an average would you say that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I trained karate, while I trained karate or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you trained karate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I said that two to three times, maybe sometimes more, sometimes less, but that is the average.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew his wife.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was her name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where she worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She worked as a nurse in a medical centre in Kozarusa as far as I know, and then in Trnopolje and in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know if Dule Tadic had any businesses in the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had for a while a cafe.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where that was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I cannot hear the interpretation well? In the main street in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have the volume increased. When you say in the main street of Kozarac, if we are talking about the main street and we have this school Rade Kondic school on the one side and the Mutnik Mosque on the other, which side of Mr. Tadic's street were they on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the side of the mosque, just on the on the right side of the main street when you go up from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "up" you mean when you go up in the direction of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the buildings or businesses that were located across the street in about the same area as Mr. Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which businesses do you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a little down -- there was a pharmacy and then up from that was a hair salon and directly across from Tadic's cafe was a building of a residential building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of this cafe that Mr. Tadic had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nipon.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever go to that cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Tadic -- during the time that you knew him did you ever see him with facial hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Often.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see him when he was clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe so.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you notice anything characteristic about the way Dusko Tadic walked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His walk was different from the rest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you describe in what way it was different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His shoulders were a bit wider and he was a bit shorter and, to speak plainly, to use, he was walking like an apprentice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I do not know what you mean by "an apprentice"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is like, I do not know how to express it, it is like a person who is full of himself because people in Kozarac gave him everything so that he can be in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to the attack on ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Miss Hollis, before you get into another area we will stand in recess until 2.30. (1.00 p.m.) (Luncheon Adjournment). (2.30 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you continue with Mr. Grozdanic?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, in response to the questions that your Honour has asked earlier, we have found either evidence or a witness who will answer those questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Miss Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we begin with this witness we have one additional quick matter and that is the Prosecution had also requested additional redactions of sensitive matters. Those were at 12.41.38, which was line 3 of page 38, 12.43.46, which was page 38, line 16. It was the same type of redaction we had asked.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand that the Defence has been consulted regarding those additional redactions and there is no objection. That is approved. It will be accomplished.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, before the break we were discussing your knowledge of and relationship with Dule Tadic. In that regard I would like to ask you if you recall prior to the attack on Kozarac an incident with him that occurred on a market day in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you recall of that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it was Thursday, and with Saban Jaskic I was checking the traffic in the centre of Kozarac, and Dusko Tadic came with another person in a white car, in a small Fiat, and parked on the road. I approached him as a member of the Reserve Police and asked him to park on the right-hand side in front of the shoe repair shop so as not to obstruct the traffic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic reply to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he replied as if I was a non-entity and that I was not a person who could order him a thing like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall anything else that he said to you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I told him, "I am sorry, but I am wearing a uniform and I should like you to respect what I have just said", and then he said, "A day will come when you will also disappear from here".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was before the attack on Kozarac, how long before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot specify the date, I do not really remember it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you on the date that Kozarac was attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in Koncari at a checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were there, was that area also attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of attack was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From all types, tanks, mortars, howitzers, anti-aircraft guns.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The area of Koncari that was attacked on that day, what was the ethnic group of the people who lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was your village of Grozdanici attacked that same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What damage was done to your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village was destroyed. Everything was burnt down and people taken to camps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you yourself give yourself up to the Serbs on 29th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you do with your police weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Turned it over.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that same, 29th May, were you taken to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have an escort on that trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know who that escort was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brane Balte.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where it was that he worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, about a month before it, he worked in Kozarac and then he moved to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 72 days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had you known any of the guards or other camp personnel before you arrived at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which of the camp personnel had you previously known?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Zeljko Meakic, the Camp Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How had you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was an active duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who else did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Drazenko, I knew Mima, and many others were there I knew.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know Mima?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Mima because we were close friends. We came to each other's home. He came to me and I went to him. We knew each other personally in Kozarac because he often came to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in Omarska what building were you kept in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was kept in the big garages.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could take the pointer that is on the table next to the console and if you could point to that building for the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you are talking about the large red building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could resume your seat then, please? Were you kept on the ground floor or the first floor of the garage building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have requested that copies be made of Prosecution Exhibit 130A which is the floor plan of the garage building. I would ask at this time that one of these copies of the ground floor be marked as the next Prosecution Exhibit in order which should be 271. If that could be provided to Mr. Grozdanic, please? Could that overhead projector be moved closer to him? Mr. Grozdanic, if you could look at that floor plan of the ground floor of the garage building and if you could point to the room in which you were held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the number in that room you are pointing to? There is a letter and a number, what is that?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if that Exhibit could be returned to me for this time, please? If Prosecution Exhibit 248, that is document 19-31, could be called up on the monitor, please? Mr. Grozdanic, would you look at your monitor and see if you have a photo on the monitor before you, if you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is portrayed in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It portrays the door to my dormitory.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The door that you used to enter that room, was it the small dark door that is outlined on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, how long were you held in this room which is marked on the floor plan as A17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Most of the time that you were at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held in this room which is marked on the floor plan as A17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there about 65 days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often did you go out of that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska, did you ever have to perform duties at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What duties did you have to perform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to clean outside and to butcher cows driven from Kozarac for the Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What other duties did you have to perform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to clean the red house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to the red house, did you have to clean any other buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to clean that slaughter room where we worked.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you have to clean this room you have referred to as the "slaughter room"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day, every morning we would come.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What would you find in there when you went to clean it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would find human clothes, blood, footwear and empty pistol cartridges.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often did you clean the red house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three or four times.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you find in there, those three or four times you cleaned the red house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We found mostly bodies, beaten up, dead people inside, a lot of gear with which they tortured people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever have to load any of those bodies on to anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times did you have to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember one occasion when I did it at night.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of vehicle or what did you load those bodies on to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A yellow small TAM truck which beforehand was used in the Omarska mine.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These bodies that you saw in the red house, did you notice any injuries or wounds on these bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They mostly had some clothes on, but one could see that their heads were broken, that their arms were broken.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know or recognise any of these bodies, any of these people whose bodies you loaded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, could you put it -- speak up a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, if the interpreter could please speak up a little or perhaps we can increase the volume again? Sir, the question was did you ever recognise any of these people whose bodies you found in the red house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once I recognised Vasfo Kejmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to once again stand up and come around to the front of the model. I am going to ask you to point to the structure you call the "red house" and then point to the structure you call the "slaughter" room. If you would first point to the red house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This is a small red building on the same side as the white house and across from the end of the large garage building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you would point to the slaughter room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can your Honour see what building is being pointed to? Is that the long rectangular building behind the end of the garage building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If you would then resume your seat? Mr. Grozdanic, did you see Dule Tadic when you were in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the date of either time that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember one of the days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What date was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18th June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to talk first about the time that you saw him on the 18th June. On that date in what building were you when you first saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the garage.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Tell us about that occasion when you saw him, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the morning. I was coming out of the WC, and as I came out he was moving from the direction of my dormitory towards the WC. I was somewhat caught unawares. I was frightened. I think I stopped the moment I saw him. He came up to me, caught me up by my face and asked me if I had been on the reserve police in Kozarac. I said, "No". Since I had a crew cut, I did not have any hair and I was all dirty, so I somehow summoned strength to say that I was not, that I had not been. Then he told me that I was from Hambarine and that my name was Jasmin Celic and then he left me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He told you that you were from Hambarine and that your name was Jasmin Celic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I told him that I was from Hambarine and that my name was Jasmin Celic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, I would like to provide you with the Exhibit that has been marked 271. If that overhead projector could be turned around again for the witness, please? Mr. Grozdanic, I would like you to look at that again for a moment. Then I am going to ask you to put some markings on that exhibit. If you would put that exhibit on the overhead projector, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is the overhead projector on, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now we have it. (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, you had indicated you were coming out of the WC, the water closet. Could you point to the room you were coming out of, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the number that appears on that room?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you, please, take one of the red pens there and put a "W" where you were standing when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could put a "T" where Dule was standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far away from you was Dule Tadic when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, it was a short distance, I cannot say, about a metre, metre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this incident how long in total did you see Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day, twice that day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But for this occasion only, this sighting only, how long in total did this incident last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been about a minute.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was he wearing at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if he had any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if he had facial hair or if he was clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did this incident occur in the morning or in the afternoon, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time, your Honour, I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 271.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 271 will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, later that day do you recall your friend, Mima, giving you some food and going with Mima to a location where you ate the food and spoke with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did this occur in the morning or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was Mima wearing a uniform that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of uniform was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an olive, drab uniform. It was a military olive colour uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you go with Mima to eat this food and talk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not far from the toilet, there was a dumper truck.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This is the same toilet that you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened then as you were sitting there talking with your friend and eating this food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we sat there, a military policeman came and brought a young man from Prijedor and following their conversation I thought that it was an auto mechanic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then this military policeman asked from this Mima to hand him over his baton.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then Mima asked whether I was there in the wrong place and whether I should be removed from there and he said, the military policeman said, no, that I could stay there. Then Mima told me to stay there a while longer, and so he can look if he could take me back to the room where we slept. Then he came back and he said, "Let's go slower", and he and I started and as we walked towards the toilet, I saw a man on the right, right side from the room where I was, there was a table and I saw him beating the prisoners. That man was Dule Tadic. Then I entered the toilet. He left me on the right-hand side in the toilet where he went.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Let us go back for a moment to this military policeman and this detainee. Did you recognise or know this military policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know this detainee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know him either.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So your friend left for a while, came back and then took you to the toilet. Is this the same toilet that you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then he put you or had you go into a certain place in that toilet, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it that he told you to go into?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me to the right, to stay there, not to go anywhere, whoever called me, to stay there until he came back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to show you two photographs. I would ask that these photographs be marked 272A and 272B. We have provided black and white copies to the Defence, but if they could be shown the colour copy, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, could you clarify whether the room A12 is also a toilet beside A11 which he has identified?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Your Honour, if I could provide another copy of the floor plan or, perhaps, I could retrieve Prosecution Exhibit 271, please? (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, before you look at those photographs, I want to give you back Prosecution Exhibit 271 which is the floor plan of the ground floor. I would like you to look at that for a moment and then if that could be put on the overhead projector, please? You have indicated that A11 was a toilet. Do you know what room A12 was? If you would look at A12 on the floor plan, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A12, I think, was some kind of a workshop. I never went in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: I see, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grozdanic. If 272A could be placed on the overhead projector? Could we pull out, please, and get the entire photograph? Do you recognise what is depicted on that photograph, Mr. Grozdanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is as you enter the toilet and this is where the wash basins are.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if 272B for identification could be placed on the overhead projector, please? Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It shows where you went for your bowel movements.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is this the area where you were taken by your friend when he took you into the water closet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you point to the little toilet area that you went into at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Please point to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, as you are looking at the photograph, you went into the last room on the far right of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 272A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 272A and 272B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, what happened then after you went into this one toilet in the WC?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I entered in there, this friend said to stay there and not to move until he comes back. After a short while, you could start hearing blows in where the wash basins are and people started groaning from strong pain and from blows.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that something like a pause happened again, and it felt like a year. That friend of mine, Mima, came and told me that we can start slowly towards the room where I was before he took me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started with him and as we were walking out past these wash basins, Mima went on the left side and I went on the right side. On the right-hand side under the wash basin there was a dead body. There were no signs of life on him. On the left, in a wash basin there was another body, dead body, and no signs of life. There was a blood all around him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you actually check either of these people to see if they were dead or alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not check because I was just passing as I was going back to the room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you recognise either of these two men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could not recognise them because these men were lying on the tile and they were facing down with their faces.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would like this Exhibit marked as Prosecution Exhibit 273A and B for identification. It is a colour photo copy and a black and white. If that could then be shown to the Defence and provided to the witness? (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, do you recognise what is depicted on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that a picture of the wash room area as you look from the toilet out through the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please put the black and white version of that photograph on the overhead projector? If you would again use the red pen and if you could put a No. "1" where the body was that you saw in the concrete wash basin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the picture).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could put a "2" where you saw the other body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the picture).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 273A and B for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 273A and B will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, did you and your friend then leave the toilet area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I passed two bodies, I was walking out through the door and the man who was beating the prisoners, the inmates, next to the table was walking out with a bloody iron stick through the door that was there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that you saw Dule Tadic as you left the toilet area, what was your emotional and mental state at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was frightened at that time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you do after this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started to the right towards the room, and I started running. This friend of mine, Mima, grabbed me by the arm and said, "Take it easy, he will kill us both". Then we both walked slowly. I looked towards my room and there was a military policeman there who was calling out Jasmin Hrnic, "Jasko", to come out.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you went toward your room, what were you focusing on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My thoughts were in that moment was to be a bird, to get into the room as soon as possible and to be among the people who were in that room with me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you walked toward that room were you looking around at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my gaze was just trained on the policeman and the entrance door, and I thought whether this policeman is going to tell me something, and whether I am going to manage to enter the room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see as you were close to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived in front of it, Jasmin came out -- his nickname was "Jasko" -- and a military policeman asked him, "Why did you not respond right away?" and he said, "I did not know that you were calling me out", and as I was passing he slapped him and then I entered in and went to Jasko's place.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So as you were passing who, who were you passing when Jasko was slapped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was passing the military policeman and Jasmin Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you came to that point and saw the military policeman calling out Jasmin and saw Jasko come out, were you looking around to see who else was there, if anyone, with the military policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I already said that I was only concentrating to get into this dormitory, this room, so that I would be with my friends.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, I am going to provide you with another copy of the floor plan of the ground floor. I would ask that this copy be marked Prosecution Exhibit 274 for identification. If that could be placed on the overhead projector, please? Mr. Grozdanic, you indicated earlier that your friend and you went behind a dump truck or a truck that was close to the room A11, and that after a time you proceeded from behind that truck to room A11 and that as you proceeded there you saw a man you identified as Dule Tadic beating prisoners. What I would like you to do first, please, is I would like you to take that red pen again and I would ask that you put a "W1" where you and your friend were behind that dump truck.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you could please draw the line to show how you went from that area to the water closet, A11?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please put a "T1" where you saw Dule Tadic as you walked toward the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you make a "T1", please? Thank you. At this time I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 274 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 274 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, I am going to provide you yet another copy of that floor plan which I would ask to be marked Prosecution Exhibit 275 for identification. Mr. Grozdanic, before I ask you about this floor plan, I want to ask you some questions about the circumstances surrounding your seeing Dule Tadic as you walked to the toilet. How far away from you would you say he was as you walked to the toilet and as you saw him where you marked his location on the prior Exhibit, how far away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere between 20 and 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him on this occasion, did you see a full face view of him, a profile view, his back, what could you see of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From his side, the right side of his face.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you also see his body or only his face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The face and all of the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long would you say you were able to see him as you walked back to the toilet from the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around 30 seconds to one minute.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was he wearing at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you see in his hand or hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had an iron bar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you said you saw him beating prisoners. Did you actually see him hitting people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you recognise who he was hitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not recognise because the person who he was beating was lying on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This Dule Tadic that you saw in profile, did he have facial hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like you to take the Exhibit that you have just been handed and if that could be put on the overhead projector, please? Mr. Grozdanic, as you came out of the toilet with your friend, Mima, you indicated you saw Dule Tadic. Would you please mark where you were when you came out of that toilet and saw Dule Tadic? Put a "W2", please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please put a "T2" where Dule Tadic was when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what direction was he walking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction towards the large door.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could, please, draw a line and an arrow showing the direction in which he was walking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw Dule Tadic on this occasion, how far away was he from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to see his face, his profile, or his back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only from the back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you able to identify him if all you could see was his back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because it was the third time that day that I was seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there anything else that aided you in your identification?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The way he walked.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please draw an arrow in the direction you and your friend went after you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 275 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 275 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would at this time ask that this black and white copy of the picture of the door to room A17 be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 276 for identification. This is a black and white copy of Exhibit 248 that has previously been admitted. (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, I would ask that you put this black and white copy of the photograph of the door into the room you stayed in on the overhead projector, please? If you could once again take that pen and if you could with the letter "P" mark where you saw the military policeman when you came back to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could use the letter "J" to show us where you saw Jasko as he exited the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could put "W3" where you and your friend were standing or were walking as you came up to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you went past them to go into the room, did you pass out around them or did you come in behind them on the door side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind Jasmin Hrnic's back and in front of the military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you could please draw an arrow showing the path to the door that you took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 276 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 276 will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, when you went back into this room where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to the place where Jasmin Hrnic had sat.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you went to that place did you see any writing on the wall there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Jasko written on the wall, "18.6".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to your coming back into the room at that time, had you ever seen that writing with that date "18.6" on the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Jasko Hrnic again after this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that you saw Dule Tadic at Omarska two times. I would now like to talk to you about this other time that you saw him. Do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened on that occasion when you saw Dusko Tadic at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were ordered to clean the large room, the big garage, and we did that with another inmate. When the garbage was to be thrown away into the containers, we started for the containers, and as we were coming out of our big building at the door by the white house, there were all inmates had been taken out in front of it, and water was poured and they were jumping all over them and forcing them to grunt as pigs. Then as I was coming out, I recognised Dusko Knezevic and Jovic. There were others, but I did not recognise them and I did recognise Dusko Knezevic and Jovic. We continued towards the container. Not far from us, a lad from Prijedor, a Muslim, had a wheelbarrow and in it he was driving a man beaten up in front of the white house who could no longer do what they had been asking them to do, asking him to do, and behind him was Dule Tadic carrying a fire extinguishing device in the left-hand side, and in his right hand he had the hose of the fire extinguisher. Now, as we reached the container to throw away that garbage, Dule Tadic shoved a hose into the mouth of the man lying in the wheelbarrow.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The hose, you mean the hose from the fire extinguisher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that we returned back towards the dormitory and Dusko Tadic -- Dusko Knezevic and Jovic continued to harass, to beat, to ill-treat the inmates who had to grunt as pigs and to pick the grass with their mouth.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So as you came from the garage building, as you came out of the building, the first group of people that you saw were mistreating detainees from the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was that the group that Dusko Knezevic and Jovic were among?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see them doing to the detainees as you came out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were jumping all over them, beating them and ill-treating them and all the rest that one could do. We were -- we did not dare look because we were frightened, because we were panic stricken.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated as you came back that they were making these people act as pigs. What do you mean? What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had poured water on the grass and then they forced them to pick that grass with their teeth, to munch it and to grunt as pigs do. Of course, in their plum tree orchards pigs used to do it and they had forced our people, Muslims, to do that in front of the white house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what general area were they when you saw them, Dusko Knezevic, Jovic and the others and the detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were as you head for our building, for our garage, on the right-hand side at the corner of the white house facing our building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then as you saw this you then began walking toward garbage containers, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we saw that the first time, yes, we were walking towards the garbage containers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what general area were these containers located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The container was not far away from the kitchen, in the corner.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you walked toward the containers you first saw Dule Tadic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We first saw Dusko Knezevic and Jovic down there and not far from that, as we were moving towards the container, we saw that Muslim and that man driving in a wheelbarrow and inmate beaten up and Dule Tadic following after them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what general area was Dule Tadic when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in the area of the white house, perhaps 50 metres away from us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then when you arrived at the containers where was Dule Tadic at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic -- at that moment Dule Tadic was to the side of the containers so that we could see a full part of his body.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know the name of that man who was pushing the wheelbarrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, his name was Amir and he was from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had you known this man before the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him from sight.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: There was a man in this wheelbarrow that was being pushed by Amir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: There was a man in the wheelbarrow that was being pushed by Amir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was. He was, I think he was a Muslim. I did not know him. I did not know the man in the wheelbarrow.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell if the man in the wheelbarrow was dead or alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not see that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you came out of the garage building and saw Dusko Knezevic and Jovic, how far away were they from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere about 30 to 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated when you first saw Dule Tadic that he was perhaps 50 metres from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were at the garbage containers and saw Dule Tadic put the nozzle or the hose in the man's mouth, how far away from you was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that was that distance or thereabouts, about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you saw Dusko Knezevic, did you see him in profile only, a full view of him or in the back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw him from the front.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first saw Dule Tadic, did you see him as a full view, a profile view or from the back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time we saw him we saw his right profile from the side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first saw him how long a time were you able to look at him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could after the container, but it was intermittent.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then when you were at the container and saw Dusko Tadic, how long did you look at him, if you can estimate that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About a minute.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time did you have a full body view of him, a full face view, a profile or only his back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see his whole body and his face.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was Dusko Tadic wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was also wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any weapons that he was carrying or that were on his person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say that, I did not notice weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether he was clean shaven or had any facial hair at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that you identified Dusko Knezevic and Jovic. Had you known Dusko Knezevic before you went to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long had you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him because he lived in a locality called Orlovci and I lived at Gornji Garevci and it was the adjacent place.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever play sports with him or play against him in sports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we worked together, we went to tournaments to Malo Palanciste and Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the jobs that Mr. Knezevic had held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was a farmer because he used to come to my father with a tractor to mow grass and while I was in the army he was in Kozarusa, in the club working as a waiter.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you describe Mr. Knezevic for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Knezevic was rather tall, a big man, round face, chestnut hair, brown hair.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever have any difficulty distinguishing him from Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I am going to ask the witness to move to the model and to use some yellow stickies to indicate where he was and where these individuals were at different points during this incident. So I would ask that we use the camera for this. Mr. Grozdanic if you could sit back just a bit from your microphone? Thank you. Mr. Grozdanic, I am going to ask at this time that you come around to the model again and put on these headphones. Then I am going to ask you to mark various areas. Mr. Grozdanic, first of all, I am going to ask that Miss Sutherland hand you the letter "W" and that you place the letter "W" where you were when you saw Dusko Knezevic as you came out of the garage building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you could take the letter "K" and if you could place that where you saw Dusko Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could take the letter "W1" and place it where you were when you first saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could take the letter "T" and place it where Dusko Tadic was when you first saw him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you could please take "W2" and place it where you were at the containers when you saw Dule Tadic put the nozzle in the man's mouth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if you could take "T1" and place it where Dule Tadic was when you saw him place the hose in the man's mouth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grozdanic. If you could resume your seat, please? Your Honours, we are again going to attempt to have a photograph made that will show those placements. Mr. Grozdanic, were you ever interrogated while you were at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first day I arrived, immediately, and once a policeman from Banja Luka came who took me for interrogation, and the last time when they took me to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During these interrogations were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second time I was taken by those mottled ones from Banja Luka, "sarenci" as we called them, and they provoked me all the night, beat me, put their knife into my mouth, a pistol to my ears and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You say "the mottled ones", "sarenci", what are those, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We call them that because they had green camouflage uniforms and they also called themselves that. When they would be coming to the camp, they would say that "Sarenci were coming, that the mottled ones, motley ones were coming". It must have been a special unit from Banja Luka because whenever they came to the camp they came with APCs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this third occasion in the white house when you were interrogated, were you also beaten on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the people who beat you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drazenko who had taken me there to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How badly beaten were you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time they took me in, they beat me. Right as you come into the white house, there was a tiny room and in it there was a cable tied to the ceiling, and they tied it around my neck so they beat me for about two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then were you beaten after that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, then they took me out, to the white house, to the last room to the right, and ordered me to stand against a wall in the right-hand corner of the wall, and to lean against a wall with both my hands or, rather, with three fingers with my both hands. I did it and then Drazenko began to beat me there with the baton on the back, on the head, on the arms, and if I happened to put all my five fingers against the wall, then he would hit me on my hands. During a very short time, after a very short time, of about a minute or two, another guard came who always sat by the kitchen, at the corner by the kitchen. I do not know his name. He must have weighed between 70 to 80 kilogrammes, a young guy, and he entered the dormitory. He came behind my back to the other wall, and then pushed himself from that wall with both his hands and jumped with his feet against my back and Drazenko continued to beat me with a baton. As he was beating me, I could no longer after some seven or eight times when he struck me against my spine, I could not endure it any longer because the pain was excruciating and I fell to the ground. When I fell, Drazenko and that one dragged me into the middle of the dormitory and then Drazenko pulled out a knife and drew on my right shoulder a cross. Then a chap came in, another guard, and told me that he was fucking my balija mother, why were we saying that he was beating us when he did not beat us, and he kicked me in the head. I began to bleed at the mouth and nose. His tennis shoe was also bloody. He said, "Why do I have to beat him like this if I can do it otherwise?" So he came out and returned after a minute and a half carrying a rod in his hand and he struck me on the head. When he lashed me on the head, the blood spurted and I think -- I thought that my whole head was swelling, was exploding. Then another guard came in and they were dragging me around the floor in that room. They started beating me again. The one who used to jump against my back, he was beating me with a baton on the head, and Drazenko was also hitting me and putting his cigarettes out on my back. The one with the rod was hitting me on the ankles and wrists, and so they were beating me and Drazenko, as they were talking all the time, Drazenko said that he could really stand a lot and that he will either kill me or let us see how long he will endure me. I thought that it was their purpose and then, I guess, dear God gave me courage so I managed somehow to get spittle in my mouth and I pretended to faint. Then one of them said, "Oh, we have managed to beat him out of consciousness". When he said that, they gave up and then it just went through my mind where I had been, what I had passed through and how did I surrender into their hands. I saw in my mind my mother, my father. They all went through my mind. When I remembered my wife, I knew that she was pregnant, that she had stayed behind and I said, "Oh, dear Lord, what have I done to you? I will never live to see my child".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, as a result of the beating that you suffered that day, what injuries did you suffer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I still suffer the effects. My head aches, my spine hurts, my joints are painful, but the worst one is the pain in my heart. I am a Bosniak, I am a Muslim, and I have lived to bear a cross on me which I do not want, but I have it. I can prove it to all of you that I have this cross on me. It is on my right shoulder -- if the camera can show it and it is here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, were you taken from Omarska camp to Manjaca when the other prisoners were taken from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you taken to Trnopolje from Manjaca because of your poor medical condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Dule Tadic while you were at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day when 1600 people went with UNICEF and the International Red Cross to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that day where were you when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw him I was in front of the school in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic was at the corner of the school fence, not far from the shop.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was he doing there when you saw him that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was standing and watching, can it be that so many are coming out, that I had not killed more?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was he wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a PAP, a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What kind of a rifle is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall on that occasion was he clean shaven or did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would ask that this photograph and a black and white copy of it be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 277A and B for identification; the colour photo being A and the black and white being B. If the colour photo could be shown to the Defence, please, and if the technician could hook up the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, before you move into that next area, we will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.00 p.m.) (The Court adjourned for a short time) (4.20 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, before we took the recess I was asking you to look at the colour photograph and the black and white copy that are there before you, Prosecution Exhibit 277A and B. Do you recognise what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The school in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could have the black and white copy of that photograph placed on the overhead projector? If you could once again take the red pen, please, and if you could put the letter "W" where you were standing the day that you saw Dule Tadic at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could please put the letter "T" where Dule Tadic was standing the day that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The day that you saw him at Trnopolje camp, these logs in the picture were not there, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: They were not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 277A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 277A and B will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, would you please look around the courtroom and see if you see the Dule Tadic you knew from Kozarac and that you saw in Omarska and Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please point to where he is seated and tell us where he is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between the two policemen, in a white shirt.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask a proper identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness has identified the accused. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Grozdanic, where did you go from Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
