utterances.text: Prior to the attacks in opstina Prijedor that began in 1992, were you a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you a member of any organised armed Serb resistance group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the attacks began did you become a member of any such group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have concluded my questions. At this time I would like to offer into evidence two photographs that were made of the markings that Mr. Grozdanic put on the model. I would ask that they be marked Prosecution Exhibit 278A and B. A will be the portion showing the markings at the hangar of the garage building in the white house, and B will show an overlap with the white house and then show the markings by the restaurant building. These have been shown to the Defence, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Exhibits 278A and B?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination? MISS DE BERTODANO: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, it is now four years since the events that you have been telling us of today, that is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: During that time you must have seen a lot of media coverage about what happened in Omarska camp, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not interested in the media. My head is full with what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Are you saying that you have never seen any media reports concerning the events in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said once, I do not want to watch something that I once experienced. I would be the happiest if I could forget it and I cannot forget it ever.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Grozdanic, it is true that you have seen a film made by Monika Gras about Omarska camp, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not like that because my working hours are 4.30 to 9.30 and I have no time for any movies, and I want to do sports during the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, do you recall making a statement to the [redacted] police in June 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I gave a statement but I cannot remember the date or the year.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could have this marked as Defence Exhibit 26 and hand it to the witness? If I could ask you to turn to page 4 of that statement, the third full paragraph down which starts "Jedan od" do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could read out that sentence to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe that I said that.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Grozdanic, if you could first read the sentence so the Court knows what you do not believe that you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "One of those two whom I recognised later in Mrs. Gras's film as G".

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: That suggests, does it not, Mr. Grozdanic, that you watched Mrs. Gras's film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see the film of Mrs. Gras.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know who is meant by G in this court?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do not mention the name, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. MISS DE BERTODANO: Perhaps in that case I could write the name for you which you could look at and not read out? If that could be shown to the Prosecution first and then to the witness? (To the witness): Do you know that person, Mr. Grozdanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to him after you had been detained in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Did you speak to him concerning the incident you have told us about today which you say occurred on 18th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I said today about that event, nobody could tell me that because I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Grozdanic. All I am asking you is whether you ever spoke to witness G about that event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not talk to him because this person is very beaten down psychologically from everything that happened to him in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So when you say in the same paragraph of that statement, "He told us later in the Manjaca camp that he had been forced to do it", it is not, in fact, true that he told you that at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Listen, I said in my statement I do not want my statements to relate anything except for what I saw with my own eyes, and that is what I stand behind, only what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Very well. You said in your evidence that you knew the defendant Dusko Tadic well, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him, but as good as a friend that I did not know, but good enough so that I can identify him in any moment.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You went to his karate classes, he was your karate trainer, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You would have contacts with him in passing? Presumably, if you met in the street or in a bar you would greet him, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally, we all in Kozarac respected him as an athlete very much.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You would see him before the conflict on average two or three times a week, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: If I could turn then to what you have told us about what happened on 18th June. You told the Court that in the morning of that day you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: This was when you were coming out of the toilets at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You saw him and he stopped you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did not stop me, but from fear I, sort of, had a sense that I just stopped myself.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: He then asked you some questions. He asked you whether you had been on the reserve police in the Kozarac, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Did he not, in fact, ask you something more than that? Did he ask you whether you knew where someone called Elvir Grozdanic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could go back to your statement and if I could ask you to turn to page 3 of the statement and to look at the last paragraph on that page? If we go to the fourth sentence of that paragraph, which starts "Uhvatio me je", can you read that sentence out to the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "He held me by the chin and asked me if I knew where Elvir Grozdanic was. I said that" -----

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: That will do, Mr. Grozdanic. Elvir Grozdanic is your name, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So I will ask you again whether he asked you if you were a reserve policeman or whether he asked you if you knew where Elvir Grozdanic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me if I was a reserve policeman in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object at this point. This is somewhat misleading. If we look at the English translation of this, it indicates, I believe, that he asked him ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are using the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe it is also in this, your Honour. According to this statement, I believe this statement indicates that at this time in this statement the witness supposedly says that Dule Tadic asked him if he knew an Elvir Grozdanic. Then he went on to ask him something about his being a reserve policeman. So if we are going to ask about this, perhaps we should include the entire sentence. MISS DE BERTODANO: Your Honour, I have no objection to the entire sentence being read.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. So it is not a matter of there being a different translation with his reading in his language and these interpreters translating it one way and then your having the English translation which, I gather, was translated at some other time? That is not the problem. The problem is it just was not complete, is that what you are asking?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, because the question, your Honour, was did he ask this or that -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. That is fine. Go ahead and continue with the full sentence then, Miss de Bertodano. You have no objection to it. MISS DE BERTODANO: The full sentence in the English translation is, "He held me by the chin and asked me if I knew where Elvir Grozdanic was; he said the latter was a reserve policeman". Is that what it says in the Serbo-Croat, Mr. Grozdanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether that was the above named reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: I think the sense of that is the same.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In any case the witness has answered. OK. MISS DE BERTODANO: If I could put this question then, are you now saying that he did not ask you whether you knew where Elvir Grozdanic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember whether he asked me. As far as I know, he asked me whether I was a reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Would you have been surprised if he had asked you about Elvir Grozdanic, considering that you knew him well and that was your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I said that I was not great friends with this person so that he might know my name.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, he would have known you because you had been in his karate class, would he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And what do you think, that only Elvir Grozdanic was in his karate classes and that he only knew of me?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Perhaps I will leave that there. You then went on to tell us about what happened later in the afternoon. You said that your friend, a guard called Mima, gave you some food, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: There were several different shifts of guards at Omarska, were there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Do you know whose shift Mima was on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not want to say that for his own security sake.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask you then whether Mima was on Krkan's shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe he was.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: I would be happier if you could give me a "yes" or a "no" answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already said because of his security I would not like to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Very well. He brought you some food and he took you to a place beside a dumper truck to eat it, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You drew for us a diagram of where that truck was and it was very close to the main door into the garage, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know from which side you are looking.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Was the truck close to the main door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. Did you understand what I asked you, the main door where we got in and out or the large door?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: The main door opposite the white house where you got in and out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Opposite the white house it was the small door and nearby and closer to the large door where the dumper truck came in and out.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Could you see the door by which you would come in and out of the hangar from where you were sitting by the trucks, and I mean the small door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was -- at that moment I was sitting behind a tyre.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So your view was blocked?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. I do apologise for interrupting, but I have a request for a redaction. It is at 16.33.06, page 78, line 22. It is one sensitive word in that sentence. I do apologise for interrupting in the midst of this. It is 16.33.06, line 22, page 78, one word. If I could perhaps provide this to Miss Featherstone so she knows what word we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection? MISS DE BERTODANO: None, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. That will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. MISS DE BERTODANO: My previous question to you, Mr. Grozdanic (which you have not answered) was whether your view of the door was blocked from where you were sitting eating your food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise one more time. I said before that I was sitting behind a tyre I could not see the door.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Thank you. At some stage a military policeman joined you and Mima and Mima went to check whether it was safe for him to take you back to your room, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: He came back and brought you to the toilets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: On your route to the toilets you looked to one side and you saw a man who you say was Dusko Tadic beating a prisoner by a table, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the table with -- not a cable but with an iron bar.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Yes. Had you while you had been sitting behind the tyre heard any sounds of someone being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was watching as the military policeman was beating the young man in front of me that he brought along with him.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Had you heard any sounds of a beating elsewhere in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, no, because this was closer.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Had you seen Dusko Tadic come into the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So the first you knew of this incident was when you were on your way to the toilets, you looked to one side and 20 or 30 metres away you saw Dusko Tadic beating a prisoner, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Was he alone or were there any other guards or soldiers with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, he was alone.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You said in your evidence that you had him in your sight for something between 30 seconds and a minute, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, how long would it have taken you to get from your position by the tyre to the toilets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: But it was very close to the toilets, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was close but it depends on how fast you are walking and how afraid you are.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: If you are afraid, do you look down or do you look around to see what is happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In every moment I look in front of me and this was in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Was it common in Omarska to watch while prisoners were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the rules, they did not want that but we found at moments we always had somebody who saw when the inmates were being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: But it was a risk, was it not, to watch while a guard was beating a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course it was risky.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You on that occasion were prepared to take that risk and watch for some 30 seconds to a minute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because in that moment I was in a position that I had to see it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: While you were watching did you see Dusko Tadic do anything else apart from beating a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You did not see him standing in front of one of the rooms and calling out some names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: If I could refer you again to the statement that you have in front of you? If you could turn to page 4 of that statement and look at the second complete paragraph? It will perhaps save time if I read the first part of that to you. "At about 5 p.m. the names of following persons were called out: Emir Karabasic, Fikret Harambasic, Eno Alic and Jasmin Hrnic". Then one sentence later: "On the way to the toilet I saw that Dusko Tadic was standing in front of the dormitory and had called out the first three names". No mention of Dusko Tadic beating anyone, simply of calling out the first three names mentioned. Is that what he did, Mr. Grozdanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. This statement in [redacted], that was totally falsely translated and, second, I never mentioned -- I gave several statements and I do not think that in any of the statements can be found that Dusko Tadic is actually calling out.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, it can be found in this statement, and this is a statement which you have signed on every page and you vouched by signing it for its accuracy. Would you like to see the original [redacted] statement and check that you have signed the pages? Perhaps I could give that statement to the witness, usher? Is that your signature on the front page of that statement at the bottom of the front page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: If you turn over the following pages, can you see your signature at the bottom of each of those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see them. But, I am sorry, I already told you the person who interpreted for me that day was a person who was not particularly fluent in [redacted] and, secondly, it was an exhaustive statement about the camp of Omarska, about everything that happened. It was not related to anyone in particular, and I know well what I said, who called out whom. All I know is that Jasko Hrnic was called out by a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Very well. You then went into the toilet and you stayed there for some time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: At some stage your friend, Mima, told you that it was safe to come back again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: In the meantime, you had been hearing noises which you took to be noises of a beating in the wash rooms outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before he came for me and called me out, those beatings, those noises and those sounds of beating were before that.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Despite the fact that you had been listening to these beatings, you thought that it would be safe for you to walk out into the area where they had been taking place, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I trusted that guy.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: As you were walking through the wash room, you saw two men lying face down with blood all around them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You told us in evidence today that you could not identify those two men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Grozdanic, you could identify them when you made the statement that you have in front of you, could you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I gave a statement. I know what it says in my statement. In [redacted], I only gave my view, my opinion. They asked me to tell them who could be that approximately and I said, well, they could have been those, but not 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So you thought that they could have been Emir Karabasic and Fikret Harambasic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: What made you think that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I thought by the size of those people lying there that it could be those persons.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Did you think that at the time as you were walking past them or did you think that afterwards when you had heard a bit more about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I returned to the dormitory, I was thinking about who it could have been and what, and then later on I heard that Emir Harambasic (sic) and all the others had been taken out and then it occurred to me that it might have been them.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So it was suggested to you by other people that the two bodies you had seen were Emir Karabasic and Fikret Harambasic, is that is right?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. He has just said he was thinking about it and he concluded that, perhaps, they were. He did not say that other people told him that. I believe the question is misleading, your Honour. MISS DE BERTODANO: Your Honour, I have the transcript in front of me. It says: "Later on I heard that Emir", I think it means Karabasic, "and the others had been taken out". I was checking whether when he said, "I heard that", he meant that someone had told him.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule the objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, not Emir Harambasic but Fikret Harambasic. Do you see well? MISS DE BERTODANO: Yes, I think there may have been a mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry once again. How many mistakes are there and you still do not believe me, and I keep saying there are mistakes. You have mistakes and so there are here. I am repeating that my statement was not properly translated in [redacted] and I do not know [redacted] well.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, it is important for this court that we check every detail of what you are telling us today and if there are differences with your statement that we give you a chance to explain those differences. I will continue by turning to the time when you are being led out of the toilet. You told us today that as you were walking through the door you saw a man 20 metres away walking away from you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You concluded that this man was Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Conclude? It was Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: He had a stick in his hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An iron rod.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: An iron stick, and you were so frightened that you started to run, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: How long had you had this man who you say was Dusko Tadic in your sight before you started to run?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not be able to say how long, but that man whom I saw and who was Dusko Tadic, it was the third time that same day that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You walked slowly back to your room after Mima had told you it was unsafe to run, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mima caught me by the hand and told me not to run, that it could be dangerous both for me and for him.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So you walked back towards your room and as you approached your room you saw a military policeman standing at the entrance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were walking towards the dormitory and we saw a military policeman standing in front of the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Apart from him, did you see any other guards or soldiers or policemen as you were walking back from the toilets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember except those two persons whom I saw, which you mentioned, and my eyes, my look was directed at that military policeman and at the door, how to enter the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You saw and heard the military policeman calling out Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Was the door to that room open or closed when he was calling for Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was open.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So was he standing by the open door and calling into the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: As you watched, Jasko Hrnic came out of that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You saw the military policeman slap him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw the military policeman slap him in the face.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Were you afraid when you saw the military policeman by the door of the room which you were heading for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why do you not try to picture yourself in that situation and then you will know whether you were afraid or not?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, perhaps you could answer me simply, were you afraid or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every normal man would be afraid.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You carried on and walked very close past them into your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Did the military policeman take any notice of you as you went past?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he already knew whom to beat, perhaps he did, but he did not address me.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Was he still standing in the doorway as you went past?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was coming towards the door, Jasmin Hrnic had already come out and as I was passing by them in the meantime he had struck Jasmin and I entered the room.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: When you entered the room did you close the door behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember doing that.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You went straight to the place where Jasmin Hrnic had previously been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: And you saw on the wall his name and the date 18th of the 6th next to the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: When you saw Dusko Tadic that day, did he have any kind of cap or hat on his head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Was he wearing any sunglasses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think that either.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, to make it clear what I am suggesting to you is this, that you did not see Dusko Tadic at all on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what you think.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: That you heard afterwards from other prisoners and later from reports in the media about what had happened in that camp on that day, and you made up this story that you yourself had seen Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much for all this, and for all this trust that you are showing. After all those atrocities I am quite ready to sit in Dusko Tadic's place and him to sit here if I have said a single lie.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: If I could turn then to the second occasion on which you say you saw Dusko Tadic in Omarska. This occasion took place after the 18th June, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember if it was before or after.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You and another person had been cleaning in the garage building and, as you were coming out of the door, you saw some inmates from the white house being beaten, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You saw Dusko Knezevic and a man called Jovic beating them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: If we look to the model we can see that from the door which you came out of to the place where you had to take the garbage to, you would have had to walk right in front of where this beating was happening, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Did you consider, as you came out and you saw the beating, that it would be dangerous for you to walk past while this beating was going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But we had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Well, was there any guard or soldier with you escorting you to where you were taking the garbage to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You did not mention that previously. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody asked me that.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Can you remember who the guard who was escorting you was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So you walked on towards the containers for the garbage and, as you were walking, you saw a Muslim with a wheelbarrow accompanied by Dusko Tadic with a fire extinguisher and a hose, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: In the wheelbarrow was a person who you say was still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that he was still alive. I do not know. I said I did not know whether he was still alive or not.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Very well. You saw Dusko Tadic put the end of the fire extinguisher into his mouth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Was the wheelbarrow moving when Dusko Tadic did this or had it stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had stopped not far from the container.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: The man who had been pushing the wheelbarrow, what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember what he was doing at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: You say that during this time you looked at Dusko Tadic for about a minute?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Were you afraid that he would see you looking at him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: So why did you not do what most people would do in that situation and keep your head down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps my eyes turned by themselves to see.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: For a whole minute your eyes did not turn themselves away again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say it was a minute 100 per cent. I said around a minute.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: This was a man whom you knew and who had been looking for you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: And yet you took that risk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was already there, on the way there, so what else could I do?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, you did not like Dusko Tadic very much, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you know that I did not like him?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE
utterances.text: Well, you have come to court today and told us about a parking incident which you considered to be important enough to give as evidence in this court during which you had had a quarrel with Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day I was not sent to quarrel with anyone, but only to control the traffic in the high street and I had asked Mr. Tadic to remove his car from the road. MISS DE BERTODANO: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Redirect.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Before I do that, your Honour, there are several places I would like to note a sensitive word for redaction.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The first one was at 16.59, your Honour, page 87 line 8, one word, 16.59.00. The second one was 16.58.18 page 87 line one, one word. After that 16.59.00, page 87 line 8, one word. Then 17.03.16 page 88 line 17, one word. At 17.05.54 there is one word in the line and I will get that in a moment. The next is 17.05.56, page 89 lines 23/24, one word. Page 89 line 23 is 17.05.54.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to those? MISS DE BERTODANO: No objection to any of those, your Honour. I apologise for them slipping in.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No problem. That redaction will be granted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: We think there may be one at 17.00.40 page 87 line 19.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The same situation?

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: The same situation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection? No objection. Those will be redacted. If possible we would like to finish this witness today, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I have very few questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grozdanic, how old were you when you took the karate classes from Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 10 or 12. I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are you of the same generation as Dule Tadic or are you of a younger generation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A younger generation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw Dule Tadic at Omarska on 18th June was your physical appearance on that date the same as it had been in Kozarac before the attacks on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the difference in your physical appearance on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I looked -- I had a crew cut. My clothes were all torn. I was dirty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You say you had a crew cut. Did you have any hair at all on your head or had it been shaved off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shaved off.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time to your knowledge had you lost any weight since you had been in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a kilo, a couple of kilos.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the afternoon of that same day, is it correct that your Serb friend Mima came to the toilet and got you and took you back to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mima accompanied you as you went to your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the afternoon when the second and third sightings of Dule Tadic occurred you testified to the Defence that that afternoon you did not see Dule Tadic come back into the garage, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You testified in response to a Defence question about this other sighting that you had to take this garbage out to the container. Why did you have to take this garbage out to the container?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we had been ordered to clean it. We did and we had to go and throw this garbage into a container, because had we refused to do that, what would follow? They would kill us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now you mentioned some problems in the interpretation of the statement, the earlier statement that the Defence has referred to. I want to refer you to a section of that statement which is as, I count the pages, on page 3 and I would like to read something to you and ask you if you know how this word got into the statement. There is a sentence on line 3, it begins with the first full paragraph on that page, saying: "These people who had to drink water in the field like cattle were then beaten up and when they were unable to walk put into something resembling a wheelchair and taken away."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. When they interpreted for me in [redacted] that statement the person who was interpreting it did not know the word "wheelbarrow" and that is why that person said "wheelchair".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you said "wheelbarrow", the interpreter did not know "wheelbarrow" and that is how "wheelchair" got into the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When this statement was finished it was read to me, but the interpreter repeated to me as I had told him. So she did not tell me the "wheelchair". She said a "wheelbarrow".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In this prior statement you did indicate that you had seen the accused on two occasions in Omarska, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that one of those occasions was 18th June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that on that date you first saw the accused in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that then in the afternoon you also saw the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also indicated in this statement that you saw the accused once in Trnopolje camp, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now there is language in this statement to indicate that when you saw the accused in the morning of June 18th that the accused came to you, held you by the chin and asked if you knew where Elvir Grozdanic was, and then said the latter was a Reserve Policeman. As you are testifying before the Court here today, tell the Court and tell them truthfully and honestly what do you remember Dule Tadic telling you when you saw him in the morning on 18th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me if I had been a Reserve Policeman in Kozarac and I told him I had not, that I was from Hambarine and my name was Jasmin Celic and he turned away and left.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Re-cross? MISS DE BERTODANO: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, at the beginning of your testimony or early in your testimony you said that at the time of the attack you were at a checkpoint at Koncari. That is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have heard a lot about checkpoints in evidence. What were your duties at that checkpoint? You stopped vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stopped vehicles mostly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your concern? What sorts of questions did you ask the vehicles you stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally when we stopped them we would ask for the driving licence and to check whether the vehicle was all right.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Well, was it simply a road safety check then or did you have orders as to whom you would stop and whom you would not stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we stopped all those who would come along that road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any orders about doing anything if you found out that the people were Serbs, for instance, or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was the same with everyone. If they had rifles they would be taken to the police station. Be he a Muslim or a Serb or a Croat, it was all the same for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So really the checkpoint was to search for arms, was it, to search for weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly that, but also of course those who used a car without documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss De Bertodano? MISS DE BERTODANO: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one comment before we release the witness, on the Prosecutor's witness list your witness No. 75, we were just wondering, that witness, do you intend to call that witness later on -- of course you can call your witnesses in your own order, but is there some reason why you cannot move that witness up? Mr. Niemann, you want to look at that?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No. 75, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No. 75 I think on your most recent list. If you are not certain, it was just an enquiry that we had. You can tell us about it on Tuesday. Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused? MISS DE BERTODANO: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Sir, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. The court will be adjourned until Tuesday at 10 a.m. (5.30 p.m.) (The court adjourned until Tuesday, 30th July 1996) 20 25
